title: Chern flat manifolds that are torsion-critical
author: Dongmei Zhang, Fangyang Zheng
work: Chern flat manifolds that are torsion-critical
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition (source0.tex lines 168--170, source label prop1): if the metric of a compact Chern flat manifold is non-Kahler torsion-critical, then the universal cover, which is a complex Lie group, must be semi-simple; and conversely every semi-simple complex Lie group admits a compatible left-invariant metric satisfying the torsion-critical condition, so that all of its compact quotients are non-Kahler torsion-critical; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 236--287 (one proof environment of 52 lines whose heading names the counted proposition). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context. For the converse it takes the semi-simple complex Lie group, its Lie algebra as a real Lie algebra, the Killing form and the canonical metric built from a compact real form, shows that the metric is compatible with the complex structure, and then computes the components of the torsion tensor in a unitary frame: it derives the symmetry relations of the torsion components, computes the two tensors A and B of the article in terms of those components, and concludes that A equals B equals the identity, which by the retained auxiliary lemma makes the canonical metric torsion-critical. The forward implication is supplied by the retained auxiliary lemma and its companion, which the article proves separately and which the counted proposition invokes. This is the article's main structural result on torsion-critical Chern flat manifolds, and it is the statement announced in the abstract. H2: a research-level differential-geometry proposition whose proof combines the structure of semi-simple complex Lie groups, the canonical metric of a compact real form, unitary-frame computations of the torsion components and the algebraic identities for the curvature-type tensors A and B; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
